questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve using **BODMAS** priority: Brackets first, then Multiplication, then Addition/Subtraction.

Calculate **Bracket** and **Multiplication**: (29 + 19) × 2 = 48 × 2 = 96

Group positive and negative values: (61 + 84 + 96) − (49 + 83)

Perform final calculation: 241 − 132 = 109

**∴ The correct answer is 109.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 61 + 84 − 49 + (29 + 19) × 2 − 83

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 61 + 84 − 49 + (48) × 2 − 83

⇒ 61 + 84 − 49 + 96 − 83

⇒ (61 + 84 + 96) − 49 − 83

⇒ 241 − 49 − 83

⇒ 192 − 83

⇒ 109

**∴ The correct answer is 109.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The acronym stands for **Brackets**, **Orders** (powers/roots), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**, defining the correct sequence of operations.

Priority of Brackets

Always solve the innermost brackets first in the sequence: round brackets **( )**, then curly brackets **{ }**, and finally square brackets **[ ]**.

Grouping Method

For faster manual calculation, sum all positive terms and all negative terms separately before performing the final **subtraction**.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the expression directly using the **BODMAS rule** (Bracket, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 71 + 27 − 34 + 18 + 13 + 21

⇒ (71 + 27 + 18 + 13 + 21) − 34

⇒ 150 − 34 = 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 71 + 27 − 34 + (18 × 1) + 39 ÷ 3 + 21

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS Rule**

⇒ 71 + 27 − 34 + 18 + 39 ÷ 3 + 21 (Solving **Bracket**: 18 × 1)

⇒ 71 + 27 − 34 + 18 + 13 + 21 (Solving **Division**: 39 ÷ 3)

⇒ 98 − 34 + 18 + 13 + 21 (Solving **Addition** from left to right)

⇒ 64 + 18 + 13 + 21 (Solving **Subtraction**)

⇒ 82 + 13 + 21

⇒ 95 + 21

⇒ 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The **BODMAS** rule defines the order of operations: **Brackets** ((), {}, []), **Orders** (powers, roots), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Priority of Operations

Division and Multiplication hold the **same priority** level and should be solved from left to right as they appear. Similarly, Addition and Subtraction are solved from left to right.

Simplification Tip

To minimize errors in expressions with multiple additions and subtractions, group all **positive terms** together and all **negative terms** together before final calculation.

questions.question: A contractor finds that 8 men can finish a piece of work in 12 days, while 12 women can finish the same work in 18 days. If 4 men and 6 women work together, how many days will they take to finish the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**8 men** finish work in **12 days** ⇒ **4 men** finish work in **24 days**.

**12 women** finish work in **18 days** ⇒ **6 women** finish work in **36 days**.

Time taken by **4 men** and **6 women** = (24 × 36) ÷ (24 + 36) = 864 ÷ 60.

Total time taken = **14.4 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total work capacity of **8 men** in **12 days** = Total work capacity of **12 women** in **18 days**.

⇒ 96 **men** = 216 **women**

⇒ 4 **men** = (216 ÷ 96) × 4 = 9 **women**

Total Group (**4 men** + **6 women**) = 9 **women** + 6 **women** = 15 **women**.

⇒ Total Work = **Women** × **Days** = 12 × 18 = 216 units.

⇒ Days for 15 women = Total Work ÷ Number of women

⇒ Required Days = 216 ÷ 15 = 14.4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Equivalence Formula

For problems involving different groups, use M₁D₁H₁ ÷ W₁ = M₂D₂H₂ ÷ W₂ to find the relation between efficiencies.

Inverse Proportion of Men and Days

The number of people required to complete a work is inversely proportional to the time taken (M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂).

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Total Time. If efficiency doubles, the time required to complete the same work becomes half.

questions.question: 3 (1)/(3) + 33 (1)/(15) + 333 (1)/(35) + dots + 33333 (1)/(99) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Separate the **whole numbers** and **fractions**: (3 + 33 + 333 + 3333 + 33333) + (1/3 + 1/15 + 1/35 + 1/63 + 1/99).

Sum of integers = **37035**.

The **fractional series** follows the pattern 1/[n × (n + 2)]: (1/2) × [1/1 − 1/11] = 5/11.

Final result = 37035 + 5/11 = **37035 5/11**.

**∴ The correct answer is 37035 5/11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 1/3 + 33 1/15 + 333 1/35 + 3333 1/63 + 33333 1/99

A **mixed fraction** a b/c is equivalent to a + b/c.

⇒ Total = (3 + 33 + 333 + 3333 + 33333) + (1/3 + 1/15 + 1/35 + 1/63 + 1/99)

⇒ Sum of whole numbers = 3 × (1 + 11 + 111 + 1111 + 11111) = 3 × 12345 = 37035

⇒ Sum of fractions (F) = 1/(1×3) + 1/(3×5) + 1/(5×7) + 1/(7×9) + 1/(9×11)

⇒ Using **telescoping decomposition**: 1/[n(n+d)] = (1/d) × [1/n − 1/(n+d)]

⇒ F = (1/2) × [(1/1 − 1/3) + (1/3 − 1/5) + (1/5 − 1/7) + (1/7 − 1/9) + (1/9 − 1/11)]

⇒ F = (1/2) × [1/1 − 1/11] = (1/2) × 10/11 = 5/11

⇒ Total = 37035 + 5/11 = 37035 5/11

**∴ The correct answer is 37035 5/11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Telescoping Series

The sum of a series where internal terms cancel out is found by: [1/Common Difference] × [1/First Term − 1/Last Term].

Mixed Fractions Addition

Always separate **integers** from **fractions** to simplify calculations in mixed fraction series.

Repeating Digit Sums

Sums like 3 + 33 + 333 + ... + 3(n times) can be calculated as [3 × (10ⁿ⁺¹ − 10 − 9n)] / 81 or simply by digit alignment.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS** rule to solve the expression efficiently.

First, calculate the product: 0.6 × 0.2 = **0.12**.

Then, calculate the difference: 0.85 − 0.75 = **0.10**.

Add the results: 0.12 + 0.10 = **0.22**.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 0.6 × 0.2 + 0.85 − 0.75

**Method:**

Use the **BODMAS** rule (Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction).

**Calculations:**

⇒ (0.6 × 0.2) + 0.85 − 0.75

⇒ 0.12 + 0.85 − 0.75

⇒ 0.97 − 0.75

⇒ 0.22

**∴ The correct answer is 0.22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: **B**rackets, **O**f, **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, and **S**ubtraction.

Decimal Multiplication

Multiply decimal numbers as whole numbers first, then place the decimal point based on the **total number of decimal places** in the original numbers.

Decimal Alignment

During **addition** or **subtraction**, always align the decimal points vertically to ensure correct place value calculation.

questions.question: 50³ - 20³ - 3 × 50 × 20 × 30 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression follows the **algebraic identity**: a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b) = (a − b)³.

By comparing, let **a = 50** and **b = 20**. Note that (a − b) = 50 − 20 = **30**.

Substituting these values, the expression becomes (50 − 20)³ = 30³.

30³ = 30 × 30 × 30 = 27000.

**∴ The correct answer is 27000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 50³ − 20³ − 3 × 50 × 20 × 30

**Method:** Step-by-step arithmetic **simplification**.

⇒ 50³ = 50 × 50 × 50 = 125000

⇒ 20³ = 20 × 20 × 20 = 8000

⇒ 3 × 50 × 20 × 30 = 3 × 1000 × 30 = 90000

⇒ 125000 − 8000 − 90000

⇒ 117000 − 90000 = 27000

**∴ The correct answer is 27000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity (a − b)³

The cube of a difference is expanded as (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b).

Algebraic Identity (a + b)³

The cube of a sum is expanded as (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b).

Difference of Two Cubes

The factorization of the difference of two cubes is a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

questions.question: The perimeter of a square is 28 cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Perimeter** of a **square** = 4 × **Side** = 28 cm

**Side** = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 cm

**Diagonal** = **Side** × √2 = 7√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Perimeter** of the **square** = 28 cm

**Formula Used:**

1. **Perimeter** (P) = 4 × a (where 'a' is the **side**)

2. **Diagonal** (d) = a√2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad95d0b244a9fc94915eee491aa5fef35c9f417ea2aa5a8106e0af5192fe5fc7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × **Side** = 28 cm

⇒ **Side** = 28 ÷ 4

⇒ **Side** = 7 cm

⇒ **Diagonal** = **Side** × √2

⇒ **Diagonal** = 7 × √2 = 7√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Square

The **Area** can be calculated as **Side**² or (**Diagonal**²) ÷ 2.

Relationship between Side and Diagonal

In any **square**, the **diagonal** is always √2 times the length of its **side** (d = a√2).

Pythagoras Theorem in Square

Since all angles of a **square** are 90°, the **diagonal** forms two **right-angled triangles** where **Side**² + **Side**² = **Diagonal**².

questions.question: Average age of 14 teachers is 45 years. One more teacher is included and the average rises by 2 years. What is the age (in years) of the new teacher?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New age = **New Average** + (**Initial Count** × **Average Increase**)

New Average = 45 + 2 = 47 years

Age = 47 + (14 × 2) = 47 + 28 = 75 years

**∴ The correct answer is 75 years.**

questions.question: Average marks obtained by 15 boys is 55 (Each boy has obtained distinct value of marks). If the highest marks and lowest marks obtained are removed, then the average reduces by 1. What is the average of the highest and lowest marks obtained?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **Average** of **15 boys** = 55

After removing 2 boys, the **average reduces** to 54 (reduction of 1 per boy)

Sum of removed items (H + L) = (2 × Old Average) + (New Count × Reduction)

Sum of H + L = (2 × 55) + (13 × 1) = 110 + 13 = 123

Average of **highest** and **lowest** marks = 123 ÷ 2 = 61.5

**∴ The correct answer is 61.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of boys = 15

Initial **average marks** = 55

Number of boys after removing **highest** and **lowest** = 13

New average marks = 55 − 1 = 54

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc1983aa510682d5f247834d92e330e0d6bfa75063931d97b11201fb9b027d3d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of marks for 15 boys = 15 × 55 = 825

⇒ Total sum of marks for 13 boys = 13 × 54 = 702

⇒ Sum of marks of (Highest + Lowest) = 825 − 702 = 123

⇒ Average of (Highest + Lowest) = 123 ÷ 2 = 61.5

**∴ The correct answer is 61.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

The **Arithmetic Mean** or average is the ratio of the sum of all observations to the total number of observations (Sum ÷ n).

Exclusion Principle

When values are removed from a group, the **sum of removed values** is equal to (Initial Total Sum) − (New Total Sum).

Impact on Average

If the **average reduces** after removing items, it means the average of the removed items was higher than the original average of the group.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio of 3 : 5. If the Highest Common Factor of the numbers is 18, then the sum of the numbers will be _____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **ratio parts** for the **sum** = 3 + 5 = 8 parts.

Since the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** represents the value of 1 unit in the ratio.

Sum of numbers = 8 × 18 = 144.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of two numbers = 3 : 5

**Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 18

**Formula Used:**

If the **ratio** of two numbers is a : b and their **HCF** is h, then the numbers are (a × h) and (b × h).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e9d8c40cfb3121dcf5fc416e7635693868bc6b27c2b1d7229e8c1ee996b1367.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 3x and 5x.

⇒ The **HCF** of 3x and 5x is x (since 3 and 5 are **coprime**).

⇒ Given x = 18.

⇒ First number = 3 × 18 = 54.

⇒ Second number = 5 × 18 = 90.

⇒ **Sum** of numbers = 54 + 90 = 144.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: A × B = HCF × LCM.

LCM from Ratio and HCF

If the ratio of two numbers is a : b and their HCF is h, then their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = a × b × h.

HCF of Coprime Numbers

If two numbers have no common factor other than 1, they are called **coprime** and their **HCF** is always 1.

questions.question: Six bells commence ringing together and ring at intervals of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 seconds respectively. In 20 minutes, how many times do they ring together? (including the first ringing together at commencement)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given intervals: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 seconds.

**LCM** (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30) = 300 seconds = **5 minutes**.

Number of times the bells ring together = (Total Time ÷ LCM) + 1.

Required times = (20 ÷ 5) + 1 = 4 + 1 = **5 times**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Intervals of six bells = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 seconds.

Total time duration = **20 minutes**.

**Formula Used:**

Common interval = **LCM** of individual intervals.

Number of rings = (Total duration ÷ Common interval) + 1 (to include the first ring).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0ca3714949ee495155c7459d5ce232629227aff94e5d13ac021114b0336c0b6d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of intervals:

5 = 5

10 = 2 × 5

15 = 3 × 5

20 = 2² × 5

25 = 5²

30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3 × 5² = 4 × 3 × 25 = **300 seconds**.

⇒ Common interval in minutes = 300 ÷ 60 = **5 minutes**.

⇒ Total rings = (Total Duration ÷ Common Interval) + 1

⇒ Total rings = (20 ÷ 5) + 1 = 4 + 1 = **5 times**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. In coincidence problems (bells, traffic lights), the **LCM** determines the next time all events occur simultaneously.

Commencement Rule

When the problem states "including the first ring at commencement" or "ringing together at the start", always **add 1** to the division result: (Total Time ÷ Interval) + 1.

Unit Consistency

Before dividing, ensure the total time and the common interval are in the same unit (e.g., both in seconds or both in minutes).

questions.question: Ratio of the value of profit earned on an article to the selling price of the article is 3 : 8. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit** to **Selling Price** = 3 : 8.

Let **Profit** = 3 units and **Selling Price** = 8 units.

**Cost Price** = 8 − 3 = 5 units.

**Profit Percentage** = (3 ÷ 5) × 100 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Profit** (P) to **Selling Price** (SP) = 3 : 8

**Formula Used:**

1) **Cost Price (CP)** = Selling Price − Profit

2) **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7557fa31ea72c7750c9a33d84279481a88a1ae2971a413fbf41608cab89efdd6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Profit** = 3x and **Selling Price** = 8x

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 8x − 3x

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 5x

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (3x ÷ 5x) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = 0.6 × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

Loss percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise. Formula: Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Selling Price Calculation

When profit percentage is given: **Selling Price** = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This is a key ratio for solving **Markup** problems.

questions.question: A person spends 30 percent of his money. He deposits 60 percent of the remaining money in the bank. If Rs. 2100 are remaining with him now, then how much money he had initially?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Effective Remaining Percentage** = (100 − 30)% × (100 − 60)%

Remaining = 70% × 40% = 28% of the **Initial Money**.

Given that 28% = ₹2100.

100% = (2100 ÷ 28) × 100 = 75 × 100 = ₹7500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Money spent = 30%

Bank deposit = 60% of the **remaining money**

Final remaining amount = ₹2100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44db1896b1057bd96303b5fa065a5e94e5616468f80b991e98367e79da319444.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **initial money** be ₹X.

⇒ After spending 30%, remaining money = X − 30% of X = 0.70X.

⇒ Bank deposit = 60% of 0.70X = 0.42X.

⇒ Final remaining money = 0.70X − 0.42X = 0.28X.

⇒ According to the question: 0.28X = 2100.

⇒ X = 2100 ÷ 0.28.

⇒ X = 210000 ÷ 28.

⇒ X = 7500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then the remaining value changes by b%, the net remaining value is (100 − a)% × (100 − b)% of the initial amount.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Calculations are faster using fractions: 30% = 3/10 (Remaining = 7/10) and 60% = 3/5 (Remaining = 2/5). Net remaining = 7/10 × 2/5 = 7/25.

Concept of Remaining

Always identify the **base** for each percentage calculation. If the problem states percent of **remaining**, the previous leftover value becomes the new 100%.

questions.question: A alone can do a work in 10 days. B alone can do the same work in 20 days. C alone can do the same work in 40 days. They started the work together. A and B both the left the work after 4 days. In how many days can C complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = **LCM** (10, 20, 40) = 40 units.

Efficiency: A = 4, B = 2, C = 1 (Total = 7 units/day).

Work done by A, B, and C in 4 days = 7 × 4 = 28 units.

**Remaining Work** = 40 − 28 = 12 units.

Time for C = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

questions.question: R travels from A to B. P travels from B to A. Distance between A and B is 540 km. Speed of R is 55 km/hr. Speed of P is 35 km/hr. They started travelling at the same time. After how many hours they will meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move towards each other, their **relative speed** is the **sum** of their individual speeds.

**Relative Speed** = 55 + 35 = 90 km/hr

**Time taken to meet** = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 540 ÷ 90 = 6 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance (D) = 540 km

Speed of R (SR) = 55 km/hr

Speed of P (SP) = 35 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂) [When moving in **opposite directions**]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/710ab13120cd0be418477fa565f7cad25fe85c82850e0a430ac8e0d6f1f4031d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = SR + SP

⇒ Relative Speed = 55 + 35 = 90 km/hr

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 540 ÷ 90

⇒ Time = 6 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the **same direction**, the relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Time and Distance Relation

Distance = Speed × Time. If distance is **constant**, time is **inversely proportional** to speed.

questions.question: The ratio of A and B in an alloy is 14 : 11. How much amount of A will be there in 275 kg of alloy?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio parts = 14 + 11 = 25 units.

Given total weight of **alloy** = 275 kg.

25 units = 275 kg ⇒ 1 unit = 11 kg.

Amount of **A** = 14 units = 14 × 11 = 154 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 154 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of A : B = 14 : 11

Total weight of the **alloy** = 275 kg

**Formula:**

Amount of A = (Ratio part of A ÷ Total ratio parts) × Total Weight

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f75409521439033d5f5792fb4e452e92fee8c472b1133195139b3ed63669c7ac.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total parts = 14 + 11 = 25

⇒ Amount of **A** = (14 ÷ 25) × 275

⇒ Amount of **A** = 14 × (275 ÷ 25)

⇒ Amount of **A** = 14 × 11

⇒ Amount of **A** = 154 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 154 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

If a quantity Z is divided in the **ratio** a : b, then the parts are [a / (a + b)] × Z and [b / (a + b)] × Z.

Percentage of Component

The **percentage** of a component in an alloy is calculated as: (Component Ratio ÷ Sum of Ratios) × 100.

Compounded Ratio

The **compounded ratio** of two ratios (a : b) and (c : d) is (ac : bd).

questions.question: Ratio of incomes of P and Q is 4 : 9 respectively. Ratio of expenditures of P and Q is 3 : 5 respectively. Savings of P is (1/6) of his income. What is the ratio of the savings of P and Q respectively?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Income of P** = 24 units → **Income of Q** = 54 units (Ratio 4 : 9).

**Savings of P** = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 units; **Expenditure of P** = 24 − 4 = 20 units.

Since **Expenditure ratio** is 3 : 5, **Expenditure of Q** = 20 × (5/3) = 100/3 units.

**Savings of Q** = **Income** − **Expenditure** = 54 − 100/3 = 62/3 units.

**Ratio of Savings** (P : Q) = 4 : (62/3) = 12 : 62 = 6 : 31.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Incomes** (P : Q) = 4 : 9

Ratio of **Expenditures** (P : Q) = 3 : 5

**Savings** of P = (1/6) × **Income** of P

**Formula Used:**

**Savings** = **Income** − **Expenditure**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4746a44930c96174b238b58a65732f54146b53eaa62060bdb579b70cacaeb7a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Income of P** = 4x and **Income of Q** = 9x.

⇒ Let **Expenditure of P** = 3y and **Expenditure of Q** = 5y.

⇒ **Savings of P** = 4x − 3y

⇒ Given 4x − 3y = (1/6) × 4x

⇒ 4x − 3y = 2x/3

⇒ 3y = 4x − 2x/3 = 10x/3 ⇒ y = 10x/9

⇒ **Savings of Q** = 9x − 5y = 9x − 5 × (10x/9)

⇒ **Savings of Q** = (81x − 50x) / 9 = 31x/9

⇒ **Savings of P** = 4x − 3(10x/9) = 4x − 10x/3 = 2x/3

⇒ **Ratio of Savings** (P : Q) = (2x/3) : (31x/9) = 6 : 31.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure and Savings Relationship

The fundamental equation for financial aptitude is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any one component can be found if the other two are known or given in ratio form.

Ratio Scaling

When two different ratios are given (like Income and Expenditure), they cannot be compared directly unless a common variable or a specific condition (like Savings of P) relates them.

Fractional Savings

If savings is a fraction 'k' of income, then Expenditure = (1 − k) × Income. This helps in directly establishing the relationship between the two ratios.
